claims.text: Adding zirconium to a refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance.
Zirconium addition will cause stable zirconium oxides to form on the alloy surface.
Zirconium reacts with oxygen to form an oxide layer.
The zirconium-containing oxide layer is protective.
The zirconium-containing oxide layer reduces oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
Reduced oxygen diffusion enhances the alloy's oxidation resistance.
The proposed benefit should occur in an oxygen-rich atmosphere at 1200°C over a 100-hour exposure.
After the specified exposure, the zirconium-containing alloy will show at least a 30% reduction in oxidation-related weight loss relative to the zirconium-free alloy.
The magnitude of the improvement may depend on the alloy's specific composition.
The magnitude of the improvement may depend on the alloy's microstructural characteristics.
The hypothesis is restricted to refractory high-entropy alloys under the stated temperature condition.
A zirconium-containing alloy and a zirconium-free control will be compared under identical oxygen-rich, 1200°C, 100-hour exposures.
The hypothesis is falsified if zirconium addition produces less than a 30% reduction in weight loss relative to the untreated alloy.
